attempted_claim: Let G_q = PSL_2(q), q odd, q→∞, |G_q|=q(q^2-1)/2, minimal nontrivial complex irreducible representation dimension δ(q)=(q-1)/2. Let β(G_q)=α(G_q)/|G_q| be the density of the largest S⊂G_q with no solutions to xy=z with x,y,z∈S (not necessarily distinct). Kedlaya's transitive-action averaging gives β(G_q)≥c q^{-1/2}, while Gowers's D-quasirandom bound gives β(G_q)≤δ(q)^{-1/3}=O(q^{-1/3}). Determine the exact order of magnitude of β(G_q): is β(G_q)=Θ(q^{-1/2}), Θ(q^{-1/3}), or Θ(q^{-γ}) for some intermediate γ∈(1/3,1/2), up to absolute constants (or up to polylog(q) factors if exact Θ is out of reach)? In particular, decide whether the single-set (A=B=C) Gowers exponent 1/3 can be improved to 1/2 for this rank-one Lie-type family, and identify the extremal structure attaining it. This is an asymptotic order-of-magnitude question as q→∞; it does not ask for a finite-q exact formula nor a conditional result unless proved unconditionally equivalent.
decisive_failure: The Gowers triple-product bound is sharp and all PSL_2(q) nontrivial representation dimensions coincide at order q, so dimension-only methods cannot resolve the single-set exponent; coset-lift constructions cap at the square-root barrier; small-q verification cannot separate asymptotic scalings. No original increment or auditable adjacent result was found.
